characters.name: Selina
characters.description: At the start of the series, she is foul-mouthed Vice President of the United States who longs for more power. She becomes the 45th President of the United States at the end of season 3 when the incumbent president unexpectedly resigns. After the end of the Meyer administration, she starts a charitable foundation to end adult literacy... and AIDS... and to promote democracy. Abusive Parents: Selina's mother was cold and cruel to her, and Selina ended up treating her own daughter in much the same way. Age Insecurity: Selina has proved many times over the series that she is incredibly insecure about her age:Out of many incredibly sexist and derogatory nicknames that the general public have called her, she takes offense at the one which denigrates her sexual attractiveness to men.When Catherine announces her engagement to a lobbyist, Selina just indignantly replies that she is 48. Later when Catherine and Marjorie welcome little Richard, she hems and haws about being called a grandmother.In Season 5, she has a secret blepharoplasty operation to remove the bags from under her eyes and refuses to appear in public until she has healed from the operation. When Minna Häkkinen immediately compliments her on the cosmetic change, Selina quickly denies that she had the operation.Selina is absolutely overjoyed when she learns that the symptoms she's been experiencing in Season 6 was a minor heart attack and not the onset of menopause, even as her doctor advises her this is much more serious and she needs a cardiac stent immediately.She deliberately obfuscates her true age, which becomes a line of attack from Jonah Ryan's campaign by demanding that she show her birth certificate.Mike:[announcing Selina's funeral]The former president passed away earlier this week at the age of 76 or possibly 77 or, according to some sources, 75. Out of many incredibly sexist and derogatory nicknames that the general public have called her, she takes offense at the one which denigrates her sexual at

characters.name: Amy
characters.description: The long-suffering Vice Presidential Chief of Staff. In the middle of season 3, she is promoted to Selina's campaign manager to replace Dan after his London trainwreck, only to later briefly resign over Selina's refusal to take her advice. After the end of the Meyer administration, Amy has a brief stint as her fiancé Buddy Calhoun's campaign manager, but she quickly rejoins Selina as her personal assistant. Beleaguered Assistant. Like everyone in Selina's staff, she's are completely overworked and constantly forced to put out fires.In season 4, she can't take it any longer, tells off Selina and quits. Belligerent Sexual Tension: With Dan. The two of them dated for a week sometime before the series began and normally can't stomach one another, but they do occasionally seem to care about one another a bit more than most colleagues do.In Season 6, they have drunken sex offscreen, which results in Amy getting pregnant. Amy tries to nudge Dan into settling down with her and raising their child together, but when Dan remains oblivious to her advances, she decides to get an abortion.In Season 7,after delivering a fiery rant at Selina's expense, she’s briefly overwhelmed, pausing to wonder if this is what a real orgasm feels like In Season 7,after delivering a fiery rant at Selina's expense, she’s briefly overwhelmed, pausing to wonder if this is what a real orgasm feels like Blonde Republican Sex Kitten:Basically what she becomes when she joins Jonah’s campaign.

characters.name: Gary
characters.description: The fiercely loyal personal assistant to Selina. Berserk Button: Gary is normally a pushover, but he gets very angry when someone hurts Selina. He also flips out when Selina says that he's unimportant to her. Beware the Nice Ones: When it's discovered Andrew is cheating on Selina, Gary screams and tries to throttle the man right in a limo. Butt-Monkey: Treated as wimpy and anExtreme Doormatto Selina. Not as bad as Jonah, though,who he does show some annoyance at.Gary:[During a shooter lockdown]Get to the panic room!Sue:Every room you're in is a panic room, Gary. Establishing Character Moment: Burns his hands holding VP Meyer's hot coffee cup while she has an idle conversation. He'll go on to do similar things in later episodes.

characters.name: Dan
characters.description: The former Director of Communications for Senator Hallows, until he sabotages her in an attempt to curry favor with Selina. This gets him a job under Mike as Deputy Director of Communications for Selina. In Season 3, he is chosen to be Selina's campaign manager, which completely blows up in his face and he is quickly replaced by Amy. After the end of the Meyer administration, Dan rebrands himself "Danny" and becomes a CBS news anchor. Beleaguered Assistant: Dan is frequently overwhelmed by Selina's demands. Belligerent Sexual Tension: With Amy. The two of them dated for a week sometime before the series began and normally can't stomach one another, but they do occasionally seem to care about one another a bit more than most colleagues do.In Season 6, they have drunken sex offscreen, which results in Amy getting pregnant. Amy tries to nudge Dan into settling down with her and raising their child together, but when Dan remains oblivious to her advances, she decides to get an abortion. Blunt "Yes"Gary: Every single thing you say to me is emasculating. Do you realize that?Dan: Yes. The Charmer: Subverted. Whenever he turns on the charm, his colleagues find it anything but.Mike:You know, Dan, watching you try to be nice is like watching a baby smoke a cigarette. It's kind of cool, but also very disturbing.

characters.name: Mike
characters.description: The rather incompetent Director of Communications for the Vice President. At the end of season 3, he becomes the White House Press Secretary. After the end of the Meyer administration, Mike briefly becomes a stay-at-home dad before joining Selina's charitable foundation. Beleaguered Assistant: He's constantly demeaned at by Selena. Big Eater: Mike is usually seen stuffing his face whenever there is food around.Jonah:Okay, Mike. One day, you're going to wake up and find that your lungs have turned into pastry.In season 4, he tries to eat more healthy at the insistence of his wife.Dan:Mike trying to be healthy. It's like a potato trying to whistle. In season 4, he tries to eat more healthy at the insistence of his wife.Dan:Mike trying to be healthy. It's like a potato trying to whistle. Brick Joke: His Bullshitzu.

characters.name: Jonah
characters.description: A freshman congressman from New Hampshire; formerly the White House Liaison to the Vice President's office, and a notorious(ly bad) womanizer. In Season 3 he is fired from the White House, but is taken back on as part of a deal. In Season 5, he's elected to Congress. Brick Joke: His obsession with getting laid by Eights. Brother–Sister Incest: Marries his former step-sister during his presidential campaign. Amazingly, the media learning of this relationship actually increases his poll numbers, even after their parents get back together.It later turns out that her father is Jonah's biological father, making them actual half-siblings. Butt-Monkey: He is hated by pretty much everyone in the Vice President's office. And the Administration. And the District. And possibly in the world. Cannot Tell a Joke: He's so inept at talking about anything that telling funny jokes is out of his league.

characters.name: Sue
characters.description: The Personal Assistant to the Vice President. Probably the most competent member of her staff. She retains her position in the Montez administration. Adults Are Useless: She doesn't do anything when Jonah reveals thathe's being sexually harassed by Teddy. Advertised Extra: Appears mostly in background scenes, either with herRunning Gagor a snark, despite being listed on the credits. She gets more screen time and a more fully-rounded character starting Season 2. Back for the Finale: After being absent from Season 6 and most of Season 7, Sue returns for the finale whereshe is back as Selina's secretary in the White House preventing Jonah and Amy from meeting with Selina. Being Personal Isn't Professional: Moreso than any other member of Selina's staff, Sue keeps her personal and professional life completely seperated. Late in season 5 she even shocks Kent with the revelation that she had been married for the past year.

characters.name: Ben
characters.description: The long-suffering White House Chief of Staff for President Hughes and his successor, Selina Meyer. He and the President were college buddies. Politics has taken its toll on him. After the end of the Meyer administration and a failed stint as a Silicon Valley consultant, Ben becomes one of Jonah's advisors. The Alcoholic: He isn't shy about it either.Amy: Anyone who talks about work tonight has to take a drink.Ben: Work.(Takes a drink) Bus Crash:He eventually passes away from natural causes sometime between the present day of theGrand Finaleand theDistant Finale. Deadpan Snarker: With the added bonus of being completely immune to any insults directed back at him (seeStopped Caring). Digging Yourself Deeper: While working as a consultant for Uber, Ben makes the mistake of using the word "Chinaman" in front of Uber's board, which has at least two East Asian people on it. When they call him out on his use of a slur, he responds with"my wife is oriental."They promptly fire him.

characters.name: Kent
characters.description: White House polling adviser and senior strategist. He was also the strategist for the President on his campaign trail and forced Selina into unwanted PR situations with her ex-husband. After the end of the Meyer Administration, Kent becomes one of Jonah's advisors. Adults Are Useless: He doesn't do anything when Jonah reveals thathe's being sexually harassed by Teddy. Badass Biker: As revealed in Catherine's documentary.In theDistant Finale, he's shown in full biker gang regalia after retiring from politics. Belligerent Sexual Tension: With Sue that seems to have been acted on but did not end pleasantly. Brutal Honesty: Kent doesn't have much of a filter. When Ellen (Mike's adopted daughter from China) says that she wants to be president of the United States, he bluntly tells her that she cannot (since one of the criteria is that you have to be born in the U.S.).

characters.name: Richard
characters.description: A bumbling young assistant who first appears on Selina's book campaign trail, and later ends up working on the Meyer campaign. In Season 4, he's promoted to Jonah's assistant in the White House. After the end of the Meyer administration, Richard becomes Selina's personal assistant. The Ace: Despite his naivety, Richard may well be the most capable person in the whole series, proving himself extremely skilled as a mayor, lietunent governor of Iowa, governor of Iowa andfinally, President wherein he is elected to two terms and is awarded a Nobel Prize for resolving the Middle East conflict and is seemingly destined to go down as one of the best in history. The Charmer: He's pretty good at winning people over and, in sharp contrast to someone like Dan, his charm is completely genuine. The Dilbert Principle: A rare positive example, Richard is incredibly inept and naïve that he is seemingly not fit for the cutthroat nature of politics. But he continues to rise in season 7 thanks to these qualities.Then for all of it, he ends up President and is actually very good at the job. Ditzy Genius: At first glance, Richard seems to be supremely incompetent; he even manages to get his own name wrong while introducing himself. However, he has two doctorates and an encyclopedic knowledge about recount procedures (which was his doctoral subject.)When he becomes President, he gets the Nobel Peace Prize for using a "three state solution" to bring peace to the Middle East.

characters.name: Catherine
characters.description: Selina's college-aged daughter, who has a contentious relationship with her mother mainly due to the latter's political career. All Lesbians Want Kids: She and Marjorie have a son after seasons of Catherine not seeming interested in having kids at all. Though she does suffer from postpartum depression. And There Was Much Rejoicing:She's positively gleeful when Selina dies, celebrating with margaritas and passing out drunk. Bourgeois Bohemian: In Catherine's defense, she wants to do genuinely good work, in contrast to Selina's self-centredness, but she was born into a family of millionaires and oligarchs, hasa degree in "interpretative dance,"and is generally quite out of touch with those who are less wealthy than she is. This is before she inherits billions herself.Catherine:Once I got used to all the regular people and how fat they were, I really enjoyed it. Butt-Monkey: Things rarely seem to go right for poor Catherine, and her mother's constant belittling certainly doesn't help. Of course, since it'sVeep, it's all played for laughs.Selina:Catherine, why is that your hair?

characters.name: Marjorie
characters.description: Selina's Secret Service body double. She later becomes Catherine's life partner. All Lesbians Want Kids: She and Catherine have a child, Little Richard, after seasons of Catherine especially seeming to have no interest in having kids. Butch Lesbian: She has a very deep voice, masculine way of dressing, and she is a soldier turned bodyguard, and she becomes Catherine's life partner. Cannot Tell a Joke: Her jokes about how Selina "gave herAIDS"noteReferring to how Selina publically announced that her charitable foundation, which she has Marjorie run, is going to doAIDScharity work without consulting with Marjorie firstfall flat because her deadpan manner makes everyone who hears it worry that she's being serious. Closet Key: She is this to Catherine. Catherine admits to Selina that the reason none of her previous relationships with men worked out was because she didn't realize she was gay which she awakened to when Marjorie asked her out.

characters.name: Marwood
characters.description: The Speaker of the House of Representatives and a member of the opposite party. In the later seasons he is in league with Tom James and attempts to deliver James the presidency by refusing to hold another House vote, though their actions inadvertently lead Laura Montez to be elected.

characters.name: Furlong
characters.description: A highly irascible Ohio Congressman who ran and lost the election for governor of Ohio. In Season 6, he is the House Minority Leader. Deadpan Snarker: Furlong constantly makes sarcastic remarks (which are usually vicious insults). Even Evil Has Loved Ones:He's aJerkass, butthat's a secret he keeps from his wife. His wife also calls him "dad" (which is what parents tend to call each other), which suggests that he's also a father. And,despite the setting, there's never any throw-away comment regarding him being unfaithful to her.In theGrand Finale,he takes care of a wheelchair-bound and senile Will. Considering what just happened toSelina and Garyin the same episode, this really says something about Roger's character. He's aJerkass, butthat's a secret he keeps from his wife. His wife also calls him "dad" (which is what parents tend to call each other), which suggests that he's also a father. And,despite the setting, there's never any throw-away comment regarding him being unfaithful to her. In theGrand Finale,he takes care of a wheelchair-bound and senile Will. Considering what just happened toSelina and Garyin the same episode, this really says something about Roger's character.

characters.name: Pierce
characters.description: A socially awkward congressman and previously one of Selina's rivals for the presidential nomination. He is described as completely incompetent. He holds great respect for President Meyer, and helps her swing a vote against his own wishes to protect her.

characters.name: Will
characters.description: Furlong's Congressional aide. Extreme Doormat: He letsFurlonginsult him (and his wife) and push him around (and he's said that he actually does enjoy his job). He's also told Furlong that he and his wife have been struggling to have children due to his wife's small uterus, which he unsurprisingly uses as one of his insults.Taken to its logical extreme in theDistant Finale, where the now-senile Will is carted around on a wheelchair by Furlong to be the butt of his jokes.Furlong:[while insulting Jonah]But guess what? That's about as likely to happen as Will's wife putting a baby in her polyp festival of a uterus!Will's wife:Why would you tell him that?Will:I just had to tell somebody. Hidden Depths: In a deleted scene for "Kissing Your Sister", he's actually been secretly planning Furlong's death and is trying toMake It Look Like an Accident. One Name Only: His last name is never given.According to the prop auction, it'sSuckfreely. Unfortunate Names: His last name isSuckfreely, although whether that's his surname at birth orFurlongmade him change it to that is left to the viewer's imagination.

characters.name: Doyle
characters.description: A highly influential U.S. Senator and the head of the Senate Intelligence Committee. In Season 4, he is nominated to serve as Selina's vice president for the remainder of President Hughes' term. He is dropped from the ticket during the 2016 election and replaced by Tom James. The Dog Bites Back:He casts the tie-breaking vote for Laura Montez, making her the new president, after Selina lies to him one time too many. Establishing Character Moment: He's the first male DC politician we spend time with, and establishes the series' trend of portraying them as dickish, sly, and with little care for Selina or her accomplishments. Everybody Has Standards: Hefires Teddywhen he learns thathe had been sexually harassing Jonah. Teeth-Clenched Teamwork: He hates Ben Cafferty and openly mocks Selina, but agrees to try and calm down the salmonella hysteria for the good of the country.

characters.name: Tom
characters.description: A charismatic former senator who Selina chooses to be her running mate in the 2016 presidential election. The Ace: He's introduced in "Convention" as a shrewd, charismatic political operator who (initially, at least) has the respect of everyone on Selina's team. Belligerent Sexual Tension: Between him and Selina.They end up having angry sex in "Congressional Ball". Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He's outwardly charming, smart, and elegant, but repeatedly proves himself to be as cruel and uncaring as many of his peers. Most notably, once he realizes he could become president due to the hung Electoral College he has no problem backstabbing Selina. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: While he’s more manipulative and cunning than outright evil, he’s still a nasty piece of work. That being said, when Selina recruits him to run with her he’s been out of politics for a few years after voluntarily leaving his senate seat to care for his son who’d been paralyzed in Iraq. He even tells a couple of the guys that he thinks all drugs should be legal because of what he saw with his son.

characters.name: O'Brien
characters.description: An Arizonan senator from the opposite party. He is initially introduced when Team Veep is courting his support for filibuster reform, and later is his party's candidate against Selina in the 2016 presidential election. Fat, Sweaty Southerner in a White Suit: Albeit minus the white suit. He's an overweight southern man, who is first introduced tucking into a plate of ribs while meeting with Dan and Amy to discuss Selina supporting a border wall with Mexico in exchange for him backing filibuster reform.Tom James jokes that O'Brien can't be president because he's still under contract to be the mascot ofKFC. Tom James jokes that O'Brien can't be president because he's still under contract to be the mascot ofKFC. Politically Incorrect Villain:When Amy introduces herself as the VP's Chief of Staff, he jokes if he should call her a "chiefess"He compares living in a state that borders Mexico to having neighbors that come on to your property and "crap a buttload of drugs and beans" on your lawn. When Amy introduces herself as the VP's Chief of Staff, he jokes if he should call her a "chiefess"

characters.name: Montez
characters.description: A senator from New Mexico who is tapped as O'Brien's running mate. Thanks to a quirk of the electoral system, she becomes the 46th President of the United States. Chekhov's Gunman: Is mentioned early in Season 4, but doesn't play much of a role in the plot until the Senate unexpectedly makes her the next President. Fake Ultimate Hero: She wins the Nobel Peace Prize after the public credits her for freeing Tibet despite Selina being the one who brokered the deal.Towards the end of Season 6, this is revealed to the public, which causes Montez's approval rating to plummet and gives Selina the publicity boost to launch her campaign. Fauxreigner: She’s a white woman from Ohio but uses her last name (her husband was actually born in Mexico) and olive complexion to make people assume she’s a white passing Latina, including frequently using a Spanish accent on her name (pronouncing it "Lao-Rah") and lapsing intoGratuitous Spanish. Foil: To Selina. Both only became presidents due to quirks in the system and both are reprehensible and manipulative women.

characters.name: Kemi
characters.description: A senator from New York running against Selina and Jonah for their party's 2020 presidential nomination. The Ace: Prior to her presidential run and Senate appointment she already had an accomplished career as a state senator, city councilwoman, U.S. Attorney, and district attorney.She is eventually elected president for two terms and is seen as superior to Selina in pretty much every way. Catchphrase: She frequently begins her public statements with "As a woman and a woman of color..." Hero Antagonist: She seems to be one of the more altruistic politicians in the show, which makes her an easy enemy of Selina. No Celebrities Were Harmed: Her name, appearance and professional background strongly resemble then-senator and future vice presidentKamala Harris.

characters.name: Teddy
characters.description: Introduced in season 4, he is VP Doyle's Chief of Staff. The Bus Came Back: After being fired by Doyle in "Convention", he returns in "Congressional Ball" as one of the campaign managers for Jonah's opponent. Abuse is Funny When It's Male On Male: Averted. He constantlyfondles Jonah's balls as a power move in the officethroughout season 4. It's neverPlayed for Laughs, and Dan isgenuinely outraged. When Doyle finds out, he fires Teddy on the spot. Even Evil Has Standards: Teddy may be a convicted sex offender, but he quits Jonah's campaign out of horror when Jonah proposes banning math because algebra was invented by Muslims. I Did What I Had to Do: As he is being fired, he claims that everything he did was in aid of his boss, especially the sexual abuse.

characters.name: Chung
characters.description: The Governor of Minnesota and a decorated veteran of the war in Iraq, something he reminds everyone of in each of his appearances. He is established early in the series as a political rival of Selina's and in season 3 he runs against her for the party's presidential nomination. Brief Accent Imitation: Dan wrote a fake anecdote about him meeting a woman named Juanita but accidentally used the same story in a speech Selina gives the same day. When Chung wants to use this to attack Selina as a plagiarist, Dan implies he would reveal Chung never met Juanita either...Chung:Oh, I did. As I recall it went something like this...(exaggerated Mexican accent)"Meester Ching, I come to America to work. I send money home but life here is so hard for me." Everyone Has Standards: As much of vain political climber as he is, even he's put off by how Selina runs her campaign, which is why he declines being her running mate. Fake Ultimate Hero: It's heavily implied that his various glorious military anecdotes didn't actually happen, or happened very differently from the narrative he pushes. It's All About Me: Every other time he speaks he's boasting about how great he is.

characters.name: Maddox
characters.description: The Secretary of Defense. In season 3, he unexpectedly resigns from his post and runs for the presidential nomination, only to quit after a poor performance in the primary debate. The Rival: He's a rival to Selina in the race for the presidency, and unlike Selina's relationship with Chung, there's genuine animosity between the two.

characters.name: Thornhill
characters.description: A former coach of an unspecified Major League Baseball team and one of Selina's rivals for the presidential nomination. He constantly uses sports analogies to describe politics, something which greatly annoys Selina and her staff. Despite a good early start in the primaries, he later loses momentum in the race. Dumb Jock: He is not necessarily aware of many political issues, and Team Selina certainly considers him one. Sympathetic Adulterer: In-universe, right when Selina is about to expose him for previously cheating on his wife he confesses to it on live television and says that since his wife forgave him he hopes America will too.

characters.name: Buddy
characters.description: The Nevada Secretary of State, introduced during the recount arc. In season 6, he's campaigning for Governor of Nevada and engaged to Amy Brookheimer, who's working as his campaign manager to the gubernatorial race. In season 7 he is one of Selina's opponents seeking their party's nomination for president. Armored Closet Gay: His appearance in Season 7 plays up this trope, where he is the fiercest advocate for banning gay marriage, despite constantly makingFreudian Slipsabout wanting to be surrounded by men in a bathroom. Attack of the Political Ad: Averted. During his campaign for governor Buddy is extremely uncomfortable about running an attack ad lambasting his opponent's wife's history of drug use. Nice Guys Finish Last: Both politically and romantically. He wants to run a clean gubernatorial campaign and gets increasingly upset at the vitriolic attack ads Amy runs. He also believes Amy when she lies in an interview that she likes sitting at home watching Downton Abbey, and he suspends his campaign so he can spend more time. This causes Amy to dump him and go back to Washington. Sorry Ociffer: Buddy is caught driving drunk and flirting with the female officer, even going as far as to expose himself to her.

characters.name: The President
characters.description: The 44th President of the United States and the incumbent present when the series begins, he constantly ignores Selina unless he needs her as a convenient scapegoat for his latest scandal. In Season 3, he decides not to seek reelection after the First Lady attempts suicide and has to be hospitalized. At the end of the season he shocks the world by resigning before the end of his term. The Ghost: We never see or hear him, although characters are constantly talking about him or to him. The one time we see Selina go to a face to face meeting with him, it's behind closed doors. Humiliation Conga: What little we see of his presidency shows it going very poorly. He leads his party to a disastrous defeat in the midterms, he gets caught in the spy scandal, he's threatened with impeachment and then his decision not to run for reelection gets outted by Jonah. Know When to Fold 'Em: It's implied he at least partially decided to resign after FLOTUS' suicide attempt as way of getting out from under multiple scandals and leaving his presidency with what little dignity he had left. Pet the Dog: Even if it was done for partially selfish reasons, his decision to resign to care for his wife is one of the most decent things any politician does in this series.

characters.name: Minna
characters.description: A Finnish politician and stateswoman, first introduced in Season 2 as the Prime Minister of Finland. She subsequently makes appearances once a season as she moves on to an international career as an economics writer, the head of the IMF, and a high-ranking United Nations diplomat. The Comically Serious: One of her quirks is being comically blunt. Fee Fi Faux Pas: Accidentally divulges some off-the-cuff remarks from Selina about theSecond Amendmentto Jonah, who leaks it to the press. Funny Foreigner: Her other defining characteristic - she and Selina have some incredibly awkward banter over the course of the show. Once Done, Never Forgotten: In her last few appearances Minna frequently brings up that Selina voted against her nomination to be head of the IMF.

characters.name: Lu
characters.description: The Chinese President contemporaneous with the Meyer and the Montez administrations. He has an antagonistic relationship with President Meyer. Completely Unnecessary Translator: In his first appearance at Camp David, he has an interpreter on retainer in his face-to-face meetings with Selina to translate their conversations. However, he reveals at the end of the episode that he is completely fluent in English. Enemy Mine: To Selina. While the relationship between Selina and President Lu is fairly hot and cold, they both rely on cooperation and backdoor deals to further their own interests from Season 5 on. Everyone Has Standards: While he certainly doesn't complain and enthusiastically agrees to the deal,he is quite surprised that Selina would allow him to revoke Tibetan sovereignty again just in exchange for meddling in the election, given how hard she fought to make freeing Tibet her own legacy."...Are you fuckin' kidding me? Is being president in a democracy even that great [that you'd do such a thing]?" Failure Gambit:He reveals that he's been helping rig the 2020 primary in Selina's favor because he wants another Montez presidency, and Meyer is the most likely opponent for Montez to be able to beat in the general.

characters.name: Murman
characters.description: The dictatorial president of Georgia introduced when Selina is part of the international team overseeing the first free Georgian elections. He wins the election by bribing Selina but is overthrown in a military coup. The Bus Came Back: At the end of his first appearance in "Georgia" he's arrested by gun-toting officers of the new military junta, but he surprisingly returns the next season in "Oslo" saying that Russia invaded his country and reinstalled him into power.Murman:Factory reboot! Faux Affably Evil: He loves to tell long-winded stories about growing up in the Georgian countryside and is always smiling. However he's a brutal dictator who imprisons journalists and attempted to poison the opposition candidate. Politically Correct Villain: He tells a story about killing a political enemy but admits he changes her gender to a man when he tells the story because of the#MeToomovement.Selina:Chivalry isn't dead.Murman:No, her name was Svetlana and she's definitely dead.Selina:Yeah, that story does work better with a man.

characters.name: Bill
characters.description: A political campaign manager and possibly the best one. Adults Are Useless: He doesn't do anything when Jonah reveals thathe's being sexually harassed by Teddyand he just says that it's an "interesting" story but not relevant to the task at hand. The Bus Came Back: He got sent to prison at the beginning of Season 5, but came back in "C**tgate" as the campaign manager for Jonah's opponent in the congressional race. He's not happy about Meyer sending him up shit creek without a pardon. Continuity Snarl: At Jonah's congressional speech, he comments that Jonah fighting with the hecklers he hired is "more beautiful than the birth of my child". In the series finale,Amy states that she and Bill never had any children in theDistant Finale, so either Bill was just saying that as a figure of speech, Amy meant thatshedidn't have kids with Bill, or it's this trope. Deadpan Snarker: He snarks so much that people can't tell when he's being sincere.

characters.name: Andrew
characters.description: Selina's ex-husband, a property developer, to whom she was married for 12 years and with whom she still has an on-and-off again affair. Belligerent Sexual Tension: Between him and Selina. In "Andrew", during a dinner they alternate between flirting and fighting in a matter of minutes. Bus Crash:Near the end of Season 7, Selina is told that he was aboard theLabor Daywhen it sunk.However... Con Man: Is essentially this. Notably, he only ever spends time with Selina when he thinks he can exploit her, never giving her a thought otherwise. Corrupt Corporate Executive: In season 6 he tries to get the Meyer Fund into several million-dollar quid pro quos with shady foreign nationals.

characters.name: Mee-Maw
characters.description: Mother of Selina and grandmother ("Mee-Maw") to Catherine. She dies of a stroke during the 2016 recount. Doting Grandparent: By all evidence was a loving grandmother to Catherine. She even bequeaths her multiple houses and the majority of her fortune to Catherine rather than Selina. Family Honor: She had the barn at the family estate renovated into an office and "love nest" for her husband's affairs, so that he wouldn't embarrass the family by being caught in seedy motels. Racist Grandma: Selina makes multiple comments that suggest she was intolerant:"There are so many friendly and diverse faces here. And I wish that Mother were alive to see this on her property."After Catherine comes out as a lesbian, Selina wishes her mother were still alive because the shock of Catherine's sexuality would kill her. "There are so many friendly and diverse faces here. And I wish that Mother were alive to see this on her property."

characters.name: Jeff
characters.description: Jonah's maternal uncle and a major power player in the New Hampshire political scene. Almighty Janitor: Despite not holding any formal elected office (he's a lobbyist for the American Association of Retired Persons), he's somehow become the sole influencer of New Hampshire's senior-citizen vote. While that doesn't sound very important on its own, the high voter turnout of the elderly, the region's polling demographics, and New Hampshire hosting the first presidential primary in the nation all ensure that Kane isn't just crucial in deciding the state's senators and governors, he has a major influence onpresidential elections. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: He's a deeply off-putting, hateful individual, but Jeff still excels at his job (he manages to help get Jonah elected to Congress,swings multiple New England delegates at the convention to make Jonah a kingmaker), and has good instincts for who will and won't succeed.He recognizes, correctly, that Richard has what it takes to be President, though he also thinks he's "10% [too] black" to win a national election."I can elect ANYONE in New Hampshire. I could elect a Muslim AIDS virus." Catchphrase:"SHUT THE FFFFUCK UP", yelled at someone (usually Jonah) in the most guttural, vicious way possible. Churchgoing Villain: An off-handed remark seems to indicate that he goes to church on Sundays with his sister.

characters.name: Keith
characters.description: The official campaign manager of Selina Meyer's 2020 presidential campaign. Faux Affably Evil: He's always polite, smiling and cheerful...and a complete psychopath. I Have Many Names: Andrew knows him as "Luther". Obfuscating Stupidity: At first glance, he appears to be a guileless fool who'll just weigh Seina down. In reality, he's a ruthless spy for the Chinese. The Sociopath: He's utterly devoid of morality and happily orders assassinations without hesitation.

characters.name: Ed
characters.description: Butt-Monkey: Whenever he appears, he gains no respect and barely even any acknowledgment. Not even Amy seems to respect him:Ed:Everyone here doesn't hate me, right?[silence]

characters.name: Leon
characters.description: A political journalist for theWashington Post, nicknamed the "Beltway Butcher." He frequently antagonizes Mike and Dan. It's Personal: He becomes obsessed with bringing down Selina after she arranges for Iran to lengthen his imprisonment so she can free him as a publicity stunt. Towards the end of Season 6, he eventually gets fired from thePostfor exactly this reason. Jerkass Has a Point: Leon is a deeply unpleasant person, but much of the time he'sabsolutely rightabout Selina's self-serving, incompetent office. Know When to Fold 'Em: At the end of Season 6,after being fired fromThe Washington Postfor his vendetta against Selina hurting the quality of his work, Leon joins Selina's new presidential campaign, replacing Mike. Sitcom Arch-Nemesis: Amy is one for him.

characters.name: Karen
characters.description: A former Senior Adviser to Selina and an old friend of hers from her lawyer days. Chekhov's Skill: Her uncanny ability to dance around the subject without actually giving a solid answer actually becomes useful when Selina's team needs her to stall the recount. Department of Redundancy Department: Everything she says is just some sort of paraphrase of what the person she's trying to appeal to already said. Enemy Mine: Amy hates her for being an annoyingYes-Manto Selina, but she gets a hold of her to stall the vote recount. Non-Answer: Her specialty is giving absolutely zero real answers to any question asked of her, only shifting words around and repeating what's been said to her.

characters.name: Jaffar
characters.description: Aristocrats Are Evil: Very wealthy and cultured-seeming, but also hugely amoral and accommadating of evil. Arms Dealer: He mentions that his great-grandfather was one. The Bad Guy Wins: A prop (the event program ofSelina's state funeral) from the series finale identifies him asthe Supreme Ruler of Qatar, implying that he took over his country at some point.While we don't know if he's good compared to the alternatives, it doesn't leave you feeling comfortable. Big, Screwed-Up Family: Mentions he has a family member on the no-fly list, and in a major reveal, sayshe has cousins who don't like America's tall buildings. Churchgoing Villain: When he's not kicking the dog, he's usually mentioning the cultural or religious practices of Islam. That Islam forbids murder, pre-marital sex, and tyranny apparently doesn't bother him.
